chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan, who said:

I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I enter the bathhouse in the morning, and therein is the man with sexual impurity and others like that. So I stand and perform ghusl, and after I finish, their water splashes upon me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not flowing water?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الْجُنُب: One in a state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Is the water in a public bathhouse considered pure if people with major impurity (junub) are using it?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia juristic principle that flowing water (*al-ma' al-jari*) retains its inherent purity (*tahur*) despite contact with impurities, provided the three attributes of water (color, taste, smell) remain unchanged. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the common scenario of a *junub* (person in major ritual impurity) in a bathhouse to illustrate that mere presence or splashing does not render the water impure, distinguishing this from stagnant water where impurity might transfer more easily. This ruling facilitates communal worship and daily hygiene by reducing ritual burden in shared spaces.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hanan who said,

‘I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I enter the bathhouse in the morning, and therein is the man with sexual impurity and other than that. So I arise and I wash, so the water from their waters sprinkles upon me after I have finished’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is it not so that it is flowing (water)?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Hanan who has said the following:

“I once heard a man saying to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘In the morning I enter the bathhouse and there is one who has experienced sexual relation and so on. I then stand up and take Ghusl (bath) and water from them sprinkles on me after I finish.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Is it not running water?’
